text:
A year ago John Gibson was one of the best stories in Detroit: 57 games and 10.1 goals saved above expected, which is how many goals a goalie keeps out beyond what the shots he faced would usually produce. Thirteen games into this season the sign has flipped. He has allowed 41 goals on shots that usually produce 34.3, a .862 save rate behind a 4-7-1 record, and the headlines have split between The Athletic urging patience and a Yahoo Sports headline reading "Red Wings Must End the John Gibson Experiment in Net."

The damage is spread across every kind of shot, but the medium and high-danger chances are where it adds up: .654 on the dangerous ones against a league .685. One thing that hasn't slipped is his rebound control, with 8.6% of his saves leading to another quick shot (league 10.8%), a sign the technique is still there. Our talent range still puts his true save rate near league average, not where it sits now. Thirteen games is a small sample for a goalie; we'd watch whether the five-goal nights stop.
